review: 2:1 אֲדֹן שָׁמַיִם — the short construct אֲדֹן is used instead of אֲדֹנָי so the line stays at ten syllables; the full form appears at the end of the stanza's couplet.

2:5–2:8 — Psalm 31:20 is the source (מָה רַב־טוּבְךָ אֲשֶׁר צָפַנְתָּ … תַּסְתִּירֵם בְּסֵתֶר פָּנֶיךָ מֵרֻכְסֵי אִישׁ), and the Arabic's 'bounty stored for the righteous' is that verse, which is why the wording is so close to it.
3:1 אֶהֱבוּ — the imperative of אהב with the short prefix, for أَحْبِبُوا; the alternative אֶהֱבוּ־נָא would break the eight-syllable line.
3:5 וְיִתְחַזֵּק לְבַבְכֶם — Psalm 31:25 (חִזְקוּ וְיַאֲמֵץ לְבַבְכֶם); the Arabic وَلْيَتَشَجَّعْ قَلْبُكُمْ quotes the same verse.
